tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Statutory requirements for CDM not followed (e.g. F10, appointment letters) and risk HSE enforcement
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures:
BoP Contractor to be appointed as CDM Principal Designer and Principal Contractor.
[Client] managing construction and discharging Client obligations.
[Client] to hire full time HSE lead for project HSE review/compliance.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: There is a risk that the contractors selected to be appointed as the key CDM roles, including the Principal Designer and the Principal Contractor do not follow the CDM Regulations 2015 requirements risking health and safety issues, incidents, RIDDORs, improperly managed Project and risks enforcement by the HSE. This is particularly the case if any appointments are subcontracted by the BoP Contractor.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures:
Procurement strategy to be sufficiently stringent to ensure the selected contractors can adequately perform their duties in line with the CDM Regulations 2015 and all duty holders are experienced in these types of construction projects.

HAZOP design review to go ahead.

[Client] to hire full time HSE lead for project HSE review/compliance.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: General construction HSE incident
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures:
To mitigate ensure a strong health and safety culture is instilled on Site by the Project team and encourage all to report near misses and share lessons learnt.
Monitor health and safety on Site by way of audits/inspections.
As above, ensure CDM Regulations appointments are made and that all duty holders are experienced in these types of construction projects

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Risk that common risks/issues that have arisen on previous similar projects occur.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: Implementing Lessons Learnt from previous battery project to ensure that any issues that have arisen are mitigated in this Project

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: There is a risk that the BoP Scope of Works does not cover the full scope of the Project risking variations being sought, extensions for time being sought leading to extra costs to ProjectCo and delays to the Project programme
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: Ensure BoP Contract scope covers all required elements.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Exact location of existing services in the access road and site unknown. Risk of hitting underground services. Service information provided in PCI.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: Ensure that risk of exisiting services sits with BoP Contractor given the terms of the ERs. DNO to take on risk associated with connection route/contestable works. BoP Contractor and DNO to validate services information provided.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Archaeology survey not undertaken prior to BoP Contract signature. Risk of encountering remains posing risk of time and cost of appropriate removal/disposal.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: Ensure that risk of archaeology sits with BoP Contractor given the terms of the ERs.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Slow internet speeds may impact commissioning the BESS on time.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures:
Managed through engaging with BT Openreach to maintain appropriate timelines. Ensure contract with BT Openreach guarantees appropriate internet speed at site.

Investigate temporary solutions for deployment incase of BT issues that need to be resolved.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Slow internet speeds may impact trading/controlling the BESS.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures:
Managed through engaging with BT Openreach to maintain appropriate timelines. Ensure contract with BT Openreach guarantees appropriate internet speed at site.
Investigate temporary solutions for deployment incase of BT issues that need to be resolved.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Failure to commence design early and/or engage in a HAZOP or early design reviews can lead to changes being made too late in the design process resulting in delays and added costs. Further, it can result in a facility being delivered to ProjectCo that cannot be operated safely or is difficult/time consuming/expensive to operate.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: To mitigate, ensure the BoP Contractor commences design work early to avoid any delays to the Project or increased costs mid-way through the Project. The BoP Contractor should also plan in advance a suitable date for a HAZOP Study as soon as possible in the Project (once the design is sufficiently advanced but not too late so as not to allow for changes to be made). Also it should be ensured that the design considers from an early stage all lessons learnt from previous projects to ensure that the design considers the operation and maintenance aspects of the facility. Ideally this should be discussed pre-HAZOP so that these issues have already been addressed.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: No fire risk assessment or engagement with insurer as yet on the design which may lead to additional requirements being needed.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: To mitigate undertake an assessment of the fire risk early and have early engagement with insurer to understand requirements for this project to ensure these are wrapped into the design and layout. Also, BoP Contractor to undertake a fire risk assessment and incorporate any requirements into the design. BoP Contractor to design to appropriate standards.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Risk of fire during construction leading to HSE risk and damage to equipment.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: To mitigate undertake an assessment of the fire risk early and have early engagement with insurer to understand requirements for this project to ensure these are wrapped into the design and layout. Also, BoP Contractor to undertake a fire risk assessment and incorporate any requirements into the design. BoP Contractor to design to appropriate standards.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Risk of fire during operation leading to HSE risk and damage to equipment.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: To mitigate undertake an assessment of the fire risk early and have early engagement with insurer to understand requirements for this project to ensure these are wrapped into the design and layout. Also, BoP Contractor to undertake a fire risk assessment and incorporate any requirements into the design. BoP Contractor to design to appropriate standards.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Vermin control becomes an issue during construction
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: Add to the BoP Contractor's scope to manage

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Vermin control becomes an issue during operation
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: Outsource: ensure contract in place with the 'rat man' to keep under control

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: There is no early earthing design assessment, therefore it is not known whether the facility will be hot or cold and therefore the impact on third party communication assets is not yet known.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: To mitigate, decision to made on the earthing design as soon as possible and appointment of any third party consultant to be made as needed.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Any design changes required following GC offer acceptance could risk the Programme.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures:
Early engagement with [DNO] to discuss/submit any potential changes.
Electrical Studies to be undertaken to validate the design.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Risk to programme - delays if outage for energisation not booked in time.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: The dates for the DNO outage for energisation and testing should be discussed with the DNO early in the Project delivery phase.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: There is a risk that [DNO] is not provided with all/complete energisation pre-requisite documentation and therefore energisation date is delayed, delaying the completion of the Project.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: To mitigate, ensure regular engagement with [DNO] and request full information from [DNO] on their requirements for energisation and ensure this is communicated to the BoP Contractor in sufficient time

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Risk of a non-compliant design
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures:
Ensure that the BoP contract captures grid compliant design as BoP Contractor liability. Electrical Studies undertaken as early as possible
, with DNO sign off to prove the design.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: DNO works programme delay to energisation would delay completion of the Project.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: To mitigate regular engagement is required with [DNO] to update on progress / programme, fortnightly calls to update on progress / programme.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: There is a risk of programme delay caused by a delay to [DNO] design approval of the substation.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures:
To mitigate, the BoP Contractor should progress with the substation design as quickly as possible and submit to [DNO] for review. Also, regular engagement is key.
GC offer to be included in PCI.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Interface of the grid connection and BoP works programmes and associated risk of one delaying the other which could impact the programme and increase costs and lead to extensions of time requests.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: To mitigate, ensure that the interface is appropriately managed with regular meetings and that an overall project programme is prepared that integrates the grid connection and BoP programmes, which can be shared with all parties.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: It is understood that crime and particularly theft of diesel and copper and vandalising of Site plant is a known issue in the area.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: Could result in several months of downtime. Accept and budget: ensure facility is adequately secure. Consult local police for advice, and consider in HAZOP. Approach to fencing and security needs to be considered during design review. Each contractor will need to take this into consideration to mitigate and take appropriate measures however, there is an ongoing risk that security issues could cause delays and extra costs with equipment needing to be re- ordered.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: It is understood that crime and particularly theft of diesel and copper and vandalising of Site plant is a known issue in the area.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: Could result in several months of downtime. Accept and budget: ensure facility is adequately secure. Consult local police for advice, and consider in HAZOP. Approach to fencing and security needs to be considered during design review. Each contractor will need to take this into consideration to mitigate and take appropriate measures however, there is an ongoing risk that security issues could cause delays and extra costs with equipment needing to be re- ordered.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Adverse weather conditions could impact the Project programme
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: To mitigate, request from the BoP Contractor sufficient monitoring of the weather forecast and subsequent rearranging of the immediate programme/tasks to mitigate impact.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Risk of control/meter/design requirements for trading on various markets not accounted for in the design.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: BoP Contract specifies that the design requirements for various markets form the scope. [Client] to ensure that BoP Contractor are comfortable with how non-specified aspects such as data transfer to/from control points and meter requirements are managed/fed into design.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: BoP Contractor have flagged that they are exceptionally busy with various projects, including non-[Client] works. Risk that BoP Contractor take on too much at once and subsequently impacts programmes.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: Ensure regular engagement with BoP Contractor to understand any risk to programme as early as possible and to keep BoP Contractor generally engaged with this project.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Any delays as a result of BT Openreach
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures:
Managed through engaging with BT Openreach to maintain appropriate timelines.
Investigate temporary solutions for deployment incase of BT delays.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Project delays could lead to initiation of when degradation would be counted from whilst the battery cells are still in storage. Would also need to ensure that warranted conditions are maintained through this period.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: Regular engagement with BoP Contractor to control all risks of delay as far as possible. If such delays are likely, engage BoP Contractor regarding conditioned storage options.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: If design doesn't meet planning noise requirements, then additional noise mitigation solutions would need to be utilised.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: BoP Contractor to be provided with noise study that formed the planning application to feed into design. Noise testing to be undertaken following build.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Final route and design assessed - [DNO] reserve right to increase costs
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures:
Early engagement with [DNO] to discuss final route options.

Accept risk.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Offer made subject to [DNO] statement of works to NGET through Mod App. If accept connection offer [DNO] inc. scheme in Mod App - customer to pay. Additionally outcome of the Mod App may lead to delays etc. should transmission works be required prior to connection. 16. Correspondance with [DNO] and 21. Correspondance with [DNO] suggests that this has already gone through the SoW process
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: Accept risk - engagement with [DNO] required to understand the risk

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: If connection offer becomes interactive, then additional charges may apply.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: Accept risk - engagement with [DNO] required to understand the risk.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Currently full power in 1 second defined in GCA - needs 0.5 seconds for DC.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: [DNO] state we need to engage with a PQ Consultant to confirm effect of 0.5 seconds ramp rate on the network. Impact to be communicated to [DNO] through studies. Ensure included in BoP Contractor/Supply Contractor package.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained:
Additional studies required as per the Grid Connection Offer than that proposed by BoP Contractor. Risk that required studies are
missed.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: Engage BoP Contractor to ensure that they understand the studies required for compliance

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Uncertainty whether road closure permits/traffic management of road works are included in initial grid offer costs. Looks like this might be an extra as per section 4.5
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: Accept risk - engagement with [DNO] required to understand the risk.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: Timelines - numerous timeline conditions to be adhered to. Land lease option to purchase or lease land secured within 2 months of acceptance form. Connection works commenced within 6 months of planning permission date. Connection works finished within 12 months of starting. Risk of non-compliance with these requirements with consequences.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: Factor timeline requirements into the master programme through engagement with BoP Contractor. Enagagement with [DNO] to understand what constitutes as commencement of connection works.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: [DNO] approved meter operator to be appointed by Customer. [DNO] to provide customer with import/export supply number. Meter operator can be [DNO]. Risk of delays to billing meter equipment/provider. Billing meter provision does not fall under BoP Contractor's scope.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: Engage billing meter suppliers and operators early to conicide with the master programme.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: As per grid connection offer, Customer Safety Coordinator Required. Safety Coordinator to be established early to avoid delays to programme.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: Ensure that the BoP Contract includes this role within it's scope. If not, to enage early with 3rd parties regarding options.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: ERs state that Contractor shall design system such that it - "Accommodate a separate grid connection dedicated to the auxiliary power supply, and / or design, procure and install an auxiliary circuit off the main grid connection." Based on this we need to make sure that BoP Contractor aren't expecting the DNO to provide a separate LV grid connection as part of the connection offer (if the DNO isn't providing this). Risk here is that DNO don't provide separate LV connection, BoP Contractor assume they are, and provisions for an aux transformer aren't made.
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: Confirm DNO requirements and whether there will be a separate supply in DNO KO. Ensure that BoP Contractor are aware of outcome so they can make appropriate provisions.

tier1_standard.Impact Explained: In order to meet net zero reactive power requirement - what if inverters cant meet requirements - is it in ERs to provide additional kit? Think so but check
tier1_standard.Mitigation Measures: Discuss with BoP Contractor to ensure that an appropriate mitigation has been included opre-BoP Contract signature.

tier2_pattern.Impact Explained:
The site is shown on the NRW Flood map for planning to lie in the Medium Risk Flood Zone 1 for tidal flooding. The Medium Risk Flood Zone is the area described as having between a 0.5% (200 year) and 3.3% (30 year) annual probability of tidal flooding.
The latest Technical Advice Note (TAN) 15 Development Advice Map shows the Site to lie in flood zone C1, land considered to be at risk of flooding but is served by significant flood infrastructure. The site is in a TAN15 Defended Zone and commercial developments are classified as Less Vulnerable, which is permitted in Zone C1 following a satisfactory completion of the justification test and acceptability of consequences.

Records of sitting water at site, particularly on the access road to site.

Flooding during construction poses risk to programme and equipment.
tier2_pattern.Mitigation Measures:
The Site is served by significant flood infrastructure. The site is in a TAN15 Defended Zone and commercial developments are classified as Less Vulnerable, which is permitted in Zone C1 following a satisfactory completion of the justification test and acceptability of consequences. In any event please see FCA for the drainage strategy.

Engage with BoP Contractor to ensure that flooding/sitting water at site has been factored into the construction strategy.
tier2_pattern.adaptation_note: Wales-specific flood zone terminology (NRW, TAN15) and a named AOD level are Newport's own -- re-derive from the new project's own FRA/flood zone classification (EA/Flood Map for England, NRW/TAN15 for Wales, SEPA for Scotland).

There is a risk of delay to the commencement of the Project and therefore a delay to the Programme as a result should the Superior Landlord refuse to provide or take a long time to provide.

All parties to monitor government rules and announcements
